title: Tennis Elbow Rehab Program
tagline: 4-Week Plan to Reduce Pain and Restore Strength

callouts: Targets the outside of the elbow (Lateral Epicondylitis)

weeks.label: Week 1
weeks.notes:
CALM PAIN. START HEALING.
- Reduce irritation
- Begin tendon remodeling
- Restore function
WEEK 1 FOCUS:
- Eccentric lengthening of the wrist flexors
- Reduce inflammation and pain
- Maintain mobility
- Begin building tendon tolerance
ADDITIONAL TIPS FOR WEEK 1:
- Use a light weight (1-2 lbs).
- Do exercises 2-3× per day.
- Ice 15-20 minutes after any activity.
- Use heat 2-6 hours in the evening.
- Stay consistent every day.
AVOID FOR NOW:
- Repetitive gripping or twisting
- Heavy lifting or forceful wrist flexion (e.g., lifting with palm up)
- Pain-provoking activities — modify as needed

exercises.name: Eccentric Wrist Flexions (Palm Up Start)
exercises.whenToUse: Targets the wrist flexors to help the irritated tendon heal.
focus: Use the other hand to return to the top.
Mild stretch and fatigue is good. Sharp pain means reduce weight or reps.
steps: Start at the top. Palm up (supine), wrist fully extended. Use a light weight (1-2 lbs). Support your forearm on your thigh or a table.
Slowly lower down (eccentric) over 3-4 seconds to full wrist flexion.
Gentle squeeze at the bottom. Hold for 1 second to further stretch the wrist flexors. Then use your other hand to lift the weight back up to the starting position.

exercises.name: Ice After Activity
howTo: Use an ice pack or ice massage.
15-20 minutes.
After exercise, sports (tennis), typing, phone use, or any prolonged forearm activity.
You can repeat multiple times throughout the day.

exercises.name: Heat in the Evening
exercises.whenToUse: Increases blood flow and promotes healing.
howTo: Use a heating pad or warm compress.
2-6 hours at the end of the day (after all activity).
Keep it comfortable (warm, not hot).

weeks.label: Week 2
weeks.notes:
INCREASE LOAD. DEEPEN THE STRETCH.
- Build tendon tolerance
- Improve strength and control
- Reduce pain and prevent recurrence
WEEK 2 FOCUS:
- Continue eccentric lengthening of the wrist flexors
- Increase repetitions and/or resistance
- Maintain full range of motion with a controlled lower (eccentric)
- Keep the bottom stretch (supine position)
- Continue ice after activity and heat in the evening
WEEK 2 TIPS FOR SUCCESS:
- Increase to 3-4 lbs (if Week 1 was 1-2 lbs).
- Increase to 2-3 sets of 15 reps.
- Maintain the bottom squeeze (supine) each rep.
- Ice immediately after activity.
- Use heat in the evening for 2-6 hours.
- Stay consistent daily.
AVOID FOR NOW:
- Repetitive gripping or twisting
- Heavy lifting or forceful wrist flexion (e.g., lifting with palm up)
- Pain-provoking activities
- Increase weight too quickly

exercises.name: Eccentric Wrist Flexions + Bottom Squeeze
exercises.whenToUse: Targets the wrist flexors to help the irritated tendon heal.
focus: Increase weight or reps from Week 1)
Mild fatigue is good — sharp pain is a sign to reduce weight or reps

other.Load: Use 3-4 lb weight (or increase from Week 1)

steps: Start at the top. Palm up (supine), wrist fully extended. Use a moderate weight (3-4 lbs). Support your forearm on your thigh or a table.
Slowly lower down (eccentric) over 3-4 seconds to full wrist flexion.
At the bottom, gently squeeze for 1-2 seconds to further stretch the wrist flexors. Keep the palm up (supine) throughout the movement.
Use your other hand to lift the weight back to the starting position. The concentric assist can be light or none (still focus on the slow eccentric lower).

exercises.name: Ice After Activity
howTo: Use an ice pack or ice massage.
15-20 minutes.
After exercise, sports (tennis), typing, phone use, or any prolonged forearm activity.
You can repeat multiple times throughout the day.

exercises.name: Heat in the Evening
exercises.whenToUse: Increases blood flow and promotes healing.
howTo: Use a heating pad or warm compress.
2-6 hours at the end of the day (after all activity).
Keep it comfortable (warm, not hot).

weeks.label: Week 3
weeks.focus: Add a concentric phase. Build strength.
weeks.notes:
ADD A CONCENTRIC PHASE. BUILD STRENGTH.
- Improve tendon capacity
- Combine eccentric and concentric work
- Increase strength and function
WEEK 3 FOCUS:
- Add a concentric (lifting) phase with lighter weight
- Continue eccentric (slow lowering) with moderate weight
- Maintain wrist flexion stretch at the bottom (supine position)
- Increase strength, endurance, and tendon tolerance
- Continue ice after activity and heat in the evening
WEEK 3 TIPS FOR SUCCESS:
- Use 3-4 lb for eccentric (down) reps.
- Use 1-2 lb for concentric (up) reps.
- Progress to 12-15 reps per set.
- Maintain the bottom squeeze (supine) each rep.
- Ice after activity (15-20 minutes).
- Heat in the evening (2-6 hours).
- Stay consistent 2-3× per day.
AVOID FOR NOW:
- Repetitive gripping or twisting
- Heavy lifting with wrist flexion (e.g., lifting with palm up)
- Pain-provoking activities
- Increasing weight too quickly

exercises.name: Wrist Flexions: Eccentric + Concentric (Palm Up)
exercises.whenToUse: Now include both lifting (concentric) and lowering (eccentric) with a bottom squeeze.
focus: Full range of motion both directions.
Use a lighter weight for the concentric (up) and a heavier weight for the eccentric (down).
Squeeze and hold 1-2 seconds at the bottom (supine).
Mild fatigue is expected — sharp pain is a sign to reduce weight or reps.
steps: Start at the bottom. Palm up (supine), wrist fully extended. Use a moderate weight (3-4 lbs). Support your forearm on your thigh or a table.
Concentric (up): Lift the weight through full range of motion in 1-2 seconds using a lighter weight (1-2 lbs).
Pause at the top. Squeeze for 1 second. Keep control and avoid wrist deviation.
Eccentric (down): Slowly lower a heavier weight (3-4 lbs) over 3-4 seconds. At the bottom, perform a gentle wrist flexion squeeze for 1-2 seconds.

2-6 hours at the end of the day (after all activity).

weeks.label: Week 4
weeks.notes:
BUILD STRENGTH. RETURN TO ACTIVITY.
- Increase strength and endurance
- Improve control and function
- Prepare for sport, work, and daily use
WEEK 4 FOCUS:
- Progress eccentric load and volume
- Continue concentric phase with light weight
- Maintain full range of motion and bottom stretch (supine)
- Build strength, tendon capacity, and endurance
- Continue ice after activity and heat in the evening
WEEK 4 TIPS FOR SUCCESS:
- Use 5-6 lb for eccentric (down) reps.
- Use 1-2 lb for concentric (up) reps.
- Increase to 15-20 reps per set as tolerated.
- Keep the bottom squeeze (supine) each rep.
- Ice after activity (15-20 minutes).
- Heat in the evening (2-6 hours).
- Begin gradual return to tennis, work, and normal use.
AVOID FOR NOW:
- Repetitive gripping or twisting
- Heavy lifting or forceful wrist flexion (e.g., lifting with palm up)
- Pain-provoking activities
- Sudden increase in weight or volume

exercises.name: Wrist Flexions: Eccentric + Concentric (Palm Up)
exercises.whenToUse: Use heavier weight for the eccentric (lowering) and light weight for the concentric (lifting).
focus: Full range of motion in both directions.
Use heavier weight for eccentric (down) and lighter weight for concentric (up).
Squeeze and hold 1-2 seconds at the bottom (supine).
Controlled tempo — no swinging or jerky movement.
Mild fatigue is expected — sharp pain means reduce weight or reps.
steps: Start at the top. Palm up (supine), wrist fully extended. Use a heavier weight (5-6 lbs) for the eccentric.
Slowly lower down (eccentric) over 3-4 seconds to full wrist flexion using the heavier weight (5-6 lbs).
At the bottom, squeeze and hold for 1-2 seconds to maximize the stretch on the wrist flexors.
Concentric (up): Lift the weight through full range of motion in 1-2 seconds using a lighter weight (1-2 lbs).

Clinical content check for Dr. Caban: tennis elbow (lateral epicondylitis) normally involves the wrist EXTENSORS, but every tennis-elbow sheet targets the wrist FLEXORS with palm-up flexion work (and the golf-elbow sheets target the extensors). Transcribed verbatim; the two programs may be swapped on the source sheets.
sourceNotes: Read tennis-elbow-4 Week 1-4 sheets (Drive ids as listed per week). All four sheets present, no duplicates. Ice and heat cards are word-for-word identical across the four weeks. Each sheet: header (MD FIT logo, condition title, 4-week tagline, target callout), week banner with headline + 3 icon goals, WEEK N FOCUS box with anatomy illustration, card 1 = the strengthening exercise (picture captions + SETS & REPS / SETS, REPS & LOAD box + KEY POINTS), card 2 = Ice After Activity, card 3 = Heat in the Evening (both with HOW TO DO IT bullets), bottom row = tips strip + AVOID FOR NOW. Field mapping: each card's one-line subtitle (purpose line under the title) is stored in whenToUse; KEY POINTS -> focus; picture captions -> steps; HOW TO DO IT bullets -> howTo; week banner headline -> week focus; banner icons, WEEK N FOCUS bullets, tips strip and AVOID FOR NOW list -> week notes (they differ week to week). Header text is printed in ALL CAPS; titles/names converted to title case. En dashes in ranges converted to ASCII hyphens; em dashes kept. No GOAL box, key principles, daily basics or progression overview exist on these sheets, so those fields are empty.
